mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts by more than 10% within two months signals a decline in demand for new homes, which is a leading indicator of a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST decreases by more than 10% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 2% within a month indicates a strong supply-side response, which typically boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, suggests a stable economic environment conducive to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods when CPIAUCSL remains below 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 1% each within a month signals strong consumer demand and labor market health, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and PAYEMS both increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when both RSAFS and PAYEMS increase by more than 1% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% within a month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases > 0.5% and UNRATE increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances when PAYEMS decreases by more than 0.5% and UNRATE increases by more than 0.3% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over six months signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances when GDPC1 increases by more than 2% over six months.
